RFC2545-3-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-12 (independent auditor) after owner-approved lint-only edits in 96ec49327b and 4e731b2d96; the row text is unchanged and each changed unit was re-read diff by diff. srpolicy subtests gained t.Parallel (each subtest builds its own UPDATE from per-iteration loop values, no shared state); reactor units drop redundant capability.AFI/SAFI conversions and newDefaultOriginatePeer takes its local endpoint 2001:db8:1::1 and link-local fe80::1 from constants with the same values. No input byte, address or assertion changed. Verdict stands. Independently rejudged against RFC2545 Section 3's global-first, optional next-hop-entity link-local-second sentence and the current changed carriers; TestRFC2545ReceivedUnusableGlobalRefused requires exact native withdrawals for unspecified/multicast first addresses and exact announcements for usable controls, while TestRFC2545ReceivedPairSecondAddressValidated crosses Session receipt and both forwarding consumers and refuses invalid second slots before scope trimming can conceal them; capability-77 negotiation combinations retain a separate standalone-link-local control, not permission for malformed pairs; announceNextHopOctets, ValidateMPNextHop/ValidateIPv6NextHop and egressNextHopWithheld continue to enforce their applicable address roles, including final effective policy fields and family-specific mapped/VPN exceptions; the repaired compatibility fixture pins fd00::2 followed by its assigned fe80::1, and the distinct-namespace stored replay fixture requires two complete ordered-pair UPDATEs with separately owned live and explicit replay arrivals; existing configured/API/queued/commit/SR-Policy carriers remain part of the previously read composition; these assertions prove address roles/order, not the missing conditional third-party address source covered separately by 3-3/3-6; native producer halts establish binding only, not a substitute for these assertions Rejudged 2026-10-12 after commit ce62c78c3b moved peer_initial_sync_test.go around these units: the tagged functions there were re-read and are byte-identical, their assertions and fixtures still carry the evidence this note cites, and the other cited units did not change, so the verdict stands. RFC2545-3-2.note: Re-judged 2026-10-12 (independent auditor) after owner-approved lint-only edits in 96ec49327b and 4e731b2d96; the row text is unchanged and each changed unit was re-read diff by diff. srpolicy subtests gained t.Parallel (each subtest builds its own UPDATE, no shared state); reactor units drop redundant AFI/SAFI conversions and newDefaultOriginatePeer takes the same local and link-local addresses from constants. No input byte, address or assertion changed. Verdict stands. Independently rejudged against RFC2545 Section 3's length 16 for a global alone and 32 when the link-local is included; direct construction writes the selected 16/32 length and corresponding ordered bytes, and replay reconstructs the entire NextHopHex field rather than reducing it to one address; current compatibility and live/stored replay fixtures assert literal complete wire encodings including length 0x20, while global-only and invalid-width controls in the existing writer/policy composition prevent an arbitrary legal-looking address or malformed width from satisfying the rule; the changed checkRFC2545NextHops uses the actual selected IPv6 session and topology-owned Ze global/link-local, requires exact decoded one-versus-two address shapes for off-link/on-link routes, and separately reads route installation, not dataplane forwarding; the strengthened topology does not weaken any width assertion; mapped single fields, standalone negotiated link-local and RD-bearing VPN fields remain explicitly separate family/draft contracts; current native bindings and Main-observed functional evidence complement the source judgment rather than deriving it from passing names Rejudged 2026-10-12 after commit ce62c78c3b moved peer_initial_sync_test.go around these units: the tagged functions there were re-read and are byte-identical, their assertions and fixtures still carry the evidence this note cites, and the other cited units did not change, so the verdict stands. Rejudged 2026-10-15 after 34fc08f0d4 changed checkRFC2545NextHops: the one edit replaces rfc2545LinkLocal(check.Network) with linkLocalAt(check.Network, zeHostNumber); both build fe80:: plus the scenario prefix with last octet 2 (zeHostNumber = 2, prepare.go), so the expected link-local, every decoded one-versus-two address shape and every assertion are unchanged, and TestRFC2545ScenarioPreparesAsBefore pins the rendered scenario. RFC 2545 Section 3: "The value of the Length of Next Hop Network Address field on a MP_REACH_NLRI attribute shall be set to 16, when only a global address is present, or 32 if a link-local address is also included in the Next Hop field." and "The link-local address shall be included in the Next Hop field if and only if the BGP speaker shares a common subnet with the entity identified by the global IPv6 address carried in the Network Address of Next Hop field and the peer the route is being advertised to." Verdict stands.

RFC2545-3-6.note: Independently rejudged against the complete RFC2545 Section 3 inclusion sentence and its requirement that the second address belong to the next-hop entity; the changed linkLocalNextHop comment correctly distinguishes an unavailable address from proof that the common-subnet condition is false, and its current body still returns no address for nextHopRouterThirdParty; classify recognizes only connected/configured/held speaker addresses as Speaker and otherwise identifies ThirdParty; therefore configured/static/API origination or an explicit rewrite naming another on-link router solely by its global address cannot supply that router's required link-local, and substituting the speaker's own would be wrong; received complete pairs and the repaired post-policy speaker-owned-global inclusion have real address sources and remain outside this absent-source gap; their successful tests and SDK workflow do not implement third-party discovery; retain the explicit no-test gap and Partial public support
